title: Reverse Complement
description: A DNA strand is a string over `A`, `C`, `G`, `T`. Its complement swaps `A` with `T` and `C` with `G`, and the reverse complement is the complement read in reverse order. Return the reverse complement of `s`.
constraints: s consists of A, C, G and T

title: GC Content Percent
description: The GC content of a DNA string (letters `A`, `C`, `G`, `T`) is the percentage of its letters that are `G` or `C`. Return the GC content rounded down to a whole number.
constraints: s consists of A, C, G and T

title: Point Mutation Count
description: Two DNA strings `a` and `b` of the same length (letters `A`, `C`, `G`, `T`) are compared position by position. Return the number of positions where they differ.
constraints: both strings consist of A, C, G and T

title: Start Codon Position
description: A DNA string uses the letters `A`, `C`, `G`, `T`. The start codon is the substring `ATG`. Return the 0-based index of its first occurrence in `s`, or `-1` if it does not occur.

examples.explanation: The first start codon is at index 2 (-1 means none).
The first start codon is at index -1 (-1 means none).

constraints: s consists of A, C, G and T

title: Codons Before Stop
description: A DNA string (letters `A`, `C`, `G`, `T`) is read from its first letter in consecutive groups of three letters called codons; a trailing group shorter than three letters is ignored. The stop codons are `TAA`, `TAG` and `TGA`. Return the number of codons that come before the first stop codon, or the total number of codons if there is no stop codon.

examples.explanation: 2 codons come before the stop codon.
0 codons come before the stop codon.

constraints: s consists of A, C, G and T

title: Reverse Palindrome DNA Check
description: A DNA string (letters `A`, `C`, `G`, `T`) is a reverse palindrome if it equals its own reverse complement, where the complement swaps `A` with `T` and `C` with `G`. Return `true` if `s` is a reverse palindrome.
constraints: s consists of A, C, G and T

title: Purine Count
description: The nucleotides `A` and `G` are purines. Given a DNA string over `A`, `C`, `G`, `T`, return how many of its letters are purines.
constraints: s consists of A, C, G and T

title: Varint Byte Length
description: A variable-length integer encoding stores a non-negative integer in groups of 7 bits, one group per byte (the most significant bit of each byte is a continuation flag). The value `0` takes one byte. Return the number of bytes needed to store `n`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Base64 Encoded Length
description: Base64 encodes every group of 3 bytes as 4 characters, and a final group of 1 or 2 bytes is padded with `=` characters so that it also occupies 4 characters. Return the length of the base64 text for `n` bytes of data.

examples.explanation: The encoded text is 4 characters long.
The encoded text is 4 characters long.

constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Hamming Parity Bits Needed
description: A Hamming code protects `m` data bits with `r` parity bits, where `r` is the smallest integer such that `2^r >= m + r + 1`. Return `r`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Run Length Encoded Size
description: Run-length encoding replaces every maximal run of equal characters by the character followed by the run length written in decimal (even for runs of length 1); for example `aaabb` becomes `a3b2`. Return the length of the encoded text of `s`.

title: Bits To Hold Range
description: Values between `lo` and `hi` inclusive are stored as their offset from `lo`. Return the smallest number of bits `b` such that every offset fits, meaning `2^b >= hi - lo + 1` (a range with a single value needs `0` bits).
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Gray Code Value
description: The reflected binary Gray code of a non-negative integer `n` is `n` XOR (`n` shifted right by one bit). Return the Gray code of `n`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Two's Complement Byte Value
description: A signed 8-bit integer is stored in two's complement. Given `n` between `-128` and `127`, return the value (0 to 255) of the byte that stores it.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Byte Checksum Mod 256
description: A simple checksum adds all bytes of a message and keeps the sum modulo 256. Given the bytes in `data`, return the checksum.

title: Plural Form
description: Form the plural of the lowercase English word `w` with these rules, tried in order: if it ends in `s`, `x`, `z`, `ch` or `sh`, add `es`; otherwise, if it ends in `y` preceded by a consonant (any letter other than `a e i o u`), replace the `y` by `ies`; otherwise add `s`. Return the plural.

title: Acronym From Words
description: `s` is a phrase of lowercase words separated by single spaces. Return its acronym: the first letter of every word, in order, in upper case.
constraints: lowercase words separated by single spaces, no leading or trailing space

args: a b c d e f

title: Camel To Snake Case
description: Convert the camelCase identifier `s` to snake_case: every upper-case letter is replaced by an underscore followed by the same letter in lower case; every other character stays unchanged. Return the result.

title: Snake To Camel Case
description: Convert the snake_case identifier `s` (lowercase words separated by single underscores) to camelCase: remove the underscores and capitalise the first letter of every word except the first. Return the result.
constraints: lowercase words separated by single underscores, no leading or trailing underscore

title: Sentence Count
description: A sentence ends at a run of one or more consecutive terminator characters (`.`, `!` or `?`). Return the number of such runs in the text `s`.
constraints: s consists of letters, spaces and the characters . ! ?

title: Mean Pixel Value
description: A grayscale image is given as a flat list of pixel values `pixels`. Return the average pixel value rounded down.

title: Pixels Above Threshold
description: A grayscale image is given as a flat list of pixel values `pixels`. Return how many pixels are strictly greater than `t`.

examples.explanation: 2 pixels are brighter than the threshold.
0 pixels are brighter than the threshold.

title: Brightest Row Index
description: A grayscale image is stored row by row in `pixels`, each row having `cols` pixels. Return the 0-based index of the row whose pixel values have the largest sum (the smallest index if several rows tie).
constraints: pixels.length is a multiple of cols, 1 <= cols <= 100, 1 <= pixels.length <= 10000

title: Mirror Symmetric Image Check
description: A grayscale image is stored row by row in `pixels`, each row having `cols` pixels. The image is mirror symmetric if every row reads the same from left to right and from right to left. Return `true` if it is.
constraints: pixels.length is a multiple of cols, 1 <= cols <= 100, 1 <= pixels.length <= 10000

title: Local Hour In Time Zone
description: A clock in UTC shows `utcHour` (0 to 23). A time zone is `offset` whole hours ahead of UTC (negative if behind). Return the hour of day (0 to 23) shown by a clock in that time zone at the same instant.

title: Minutes Until Clock Time
description: Times are written as `HH:MM` on a 24-hour clock. Given the current time `now` and a `target` time, return the number of minutes you must wait until the clock next shows `target` (it is `0` if they are equal; if the target time has already passed today it is the next day's).
constraints: now and target are valid times between 00:00 and 23:59
All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Seconds To Clock Format
description: Return the duration of `seconds` seconds written as `HH:MM:SS`, where hours may exceed 23 and every field has at least two digits (zero padded).
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Hash Bucket Collisions
description: Keys are inserted one by one into a hash table with `m` buckets, key `k` going to bucket `k mod m` (all keys are non-negative). A collision occurs when a key lands in a bucket that already holds at least one earlier key. Return the number of collisions.

title: Polynomial Value At Point
description: A polynomial is given by its coefficients `coeffs` from the constant term upward: `coeffs[0] + coeffs[1] * x + coeffs[2] * x^2 + ...`. Return its value at `x`.

title: Polynomial Degree
description: A polynomial is given by its coefficients `coeffs` from the constant term upward (trailing coefficients may be zero). Return its degree, the largest power with a non-zero coefficient, or `-1` if every coefficient is zero.

examples.explanation: The degree is 1 (-1 means the zero polynomial).
The degree is -1 (-1 means the zero polynomial).

title: Polynomial Derivative Value
description: A polynomial is given by its coefficients `coeffs` from the constant term upward: `coeffs[0] + coeffs[1] * x + coeffs[2] * x^2 + ...`. Return the value of its derivative at `x`.

title: Polynomial Sum Degree
description: Two polynomials are given by their coefficients from the constant term upward (`a[i]` multiplies `x^i`). Return the degree of their sum, the largest power with a non-zero coefficient, or `-1` if the sum is the zero polynomial.

title: Bubble Sort Pass Count
description: Bubble sort repeatedly makes a pass over the array, comparing each neighbouring pair from left to right and swapping the two when the left one is larger. It stops after the first pass in which no swap happens. Return the total number of passes made, counting that final swap-free pass.

title: Selection Sort Swap Count
description: Selection sort works left to right: at step `i` it finds the leftmost minimum of the elements from position `i` onward and, if that minimum is not already at position `i`, swaps it into place. Return the total number of swaps performed.

title: Even Parity Byte Value
description: A 7-bit value `n` is sent as an 8-bit byte whose top bit is an even-parity bit: it is set to `1` exactly when `n` has an odd number of one-bits, so that the whole byte has an even number of ones. Return the byte as an integer between 0 and 255.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Longest Reverse Palindrome Length
description: A DNA string over `A`, `C`, `G`, `T` is a reverse palindrome if it equals its own reverse complement (the complement swaps `A` with `T` and `C` with `G`; the reverse complement reads the complement backwards). Return the length of the longest substring of `s` that is a reverse palindrome, or `0` if there is none.

examples.explanation: The longest reverse palindrome has length 6.
The longest reverse palindrome has length 0.

constraints: s consists of A, C, G and T

title: Longest Open Reading Frame
description: A DNA string uses the letters `A`, `C`, `G`, `T`. An open reading frame starts at any occurrence of the start codon `ATG` and reads consecutive groups of three letters (codons) until the first stop codon (`TAA`, `TAG` or `TGA`) in that same reading frame; the frame only counts if a stop codon is found before the string ends. Its length is the number of codons before the stop codon, counting the start codon. Return the length of the longest open reading frame in `s`, or `0` if there is none.

examples.explanation: The longest open reading frame has 2 codons.
The longest open reading frame has 0 codons.

constraints: s consists of A, C, G and T

title: Unique K-mer Count
description: A k-mer is a substring of length `k`. Overlapping occurrences count separately. Return the number of distinct k-mers of the DNA string `s` that occur exactly once in `s`.
constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 1000, s consists of A, C, G and T

title: GC Skew Minimum Position
description: The GC skew of a DNA prefix is the number of `G` minus the number of `C` in it. For a string `s` of length `n` look at the skew of each prefix of length `0, 1, ..., n`. Return the smallest prefix length at which the skew reaches its minimum value.

examples.explanation: The minimum skew is first reached at prefix length 1.
The minimum skew is first reached at prefix length 0.

constraints: s consists of A, C, G and T

title: Longest Square Substring Length
description: A square string is a non-empty string written twice in a row, such as `abab` (`ab` + `ab`). Return the length of the longest substring of `s` that is a square string, or `0` if there is none.

examples.explanation: The longest square substring has length 4.
The longest square substring has length 0.

title: Varint Stream Decode Sum
description: A stream of bytes holds non-negative integers in a variable-length encoding. Each integer is stored least-significant 7-bit group first, one group per byte: the low 7 bits of the byte are the group and the top bit says whether another byte of the same integer follows (`1`) or this is its last byte (`0`). Integers are stored back to back. Decode the whole stream and return the sum of all the integers.

examples.explanation: The decoded integers add up to 1.
The decoded integers add up to 300.

constraints: the last byte is below 128 and no integer uses more than 3 bytes

title: Base64 Encode Text
description: Encode the ASCII text `s` in base64: write the bytes as a bit string, cut it into 6-bit groups (padding the last group with zero bits on the right), map each group to a character using the alphabet `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `+`, `/` (values 0 to 63 in that order), and finally append `=` characters until the output length is a multiple of 4. Return the encoded text.
constraints: s consists of lowercase letters, digits and spaces

title: Hamming Code Error Position
description: A 7-bit Hamming code word is a string of bits at positions `1` to `7` (left to right). Positions 1, 2 and 4 hold parity bits: the parity bit at position `p` makes the total number of `1` bits among all positions whose number has bit `p` set even (positions 1, 3, 5, 7 for `p = 1`; positions 2, 3, 6, 7 for `p = 2`; positions 4, 5, 6, 7 for `p = 4`). Given a received 7-bit string, return the position (1 to 7) of the single bit that must be flipped to make all three parity checks pass, or `0` if they already pass.

examples.explanation: The error position is 0 (0 means none).
The error position is 1 (0 means none).

constraints: bits has exactly 7 characters, each 0 or 1
All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Bit Stuffing Output Length
description: In bit stuffing, after every run of five consecutive `1` bits in the data a `0` bit is inserted into the output (the inserted `0` also ends the run, so the count of consecutive ones starts again from zero). Given the data bits `bits`, return the length of the stuffed output.

title: CRC Remainder Bits
description: A cyclic redundancy check divides a message by a generator using polynomial arithmetic over bits (subtraction is XOR). Given the message bits `message` and the generator bits `gen` (it starts with `1` and has `k + 1` bits), append `k` zero bits to the message, divide that bit string by `gen` with XOR long division, and return the remainder as exactly `k` bits.
constraints: 2 <= gen.length <= 9, gen consists of 0 and 1 and starts with 1

title: Move To Front Index Sum
description: Move-to-front coding keeps a list of the 26 lowercase letters, initially in the order `a, b, ..., z`. To code a letter, output its current 0-based position in the list and then move that letter to the front of the list. Return the sum of all the output positions when coding the string `s`.

title: LZ77 Token Count
description: A simple LZ77 compressor reads `s` from left to right. At position `i` it looks for the longest match: a length `L` such that `s[j .. j+L-1] = s[i .. i+L-1]` for some start `j` with `i - W <= j < i` (the match may run past position `i`, but must stay inside the string). If the longest match has length at least 3, one token is emitted covering those `L` characters; otherwise one token is emitted for the single character at `i`. Return the number of tokens emitted for the whole string.
constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 500, s consists of lowercase letters

title: Burrows-Wheeler Transform
description: The Burrows-Wheeler transform of a string `s` is computed by appending the sentinel `$` (which sorts before every letter), writing down all cyclic rotations of the result, sorting them lexicographically, and reading off the last character of every rotation in that order. Return the transformed string, which has length `s.length + 1`.

title: Inverse Burrows-Wheeler
description: `t` is the Burrows-Wheeler transform of some lowercase string `s`: the last column of the sorted list of all cyclic rotations of `s + '$'`, where the sentinel `$` sorts before every letter. Return the original string `s`.
constraints: t is the transform of a lowercase string, so it contains exactly one $

title: Run Length Decoded Length
description: A run-length encoded text consists of items, each a lowercase letter optionally followed by a decimal repeat count from 1 to 999 without leading zeros (a letter without a count means one copy). For example `a3bc2` decodes to `aaabcc`. Return the length of the decoded text.

title: Delta Of Delta Zero Count
description: Time-series databases compress strictly increasing timestamps by storing the second difference. For timestamps `t`, the first difference at position `i` is `t[i] - t[i-1]`, and the delta of delta at position `i >= 2` is the difference between consecutive first differences. Return how many deltas of delta are exactly zero.

title: Bit Packing Words Needed
description: Values with the bit widths in `widths` are written one after another into 32-bit words, filling each word from its first bit. A value must not straddle two words: if the remaining room in the current word is smaller than the next width, the rest of that word is left unused and the value starts a new word. Return the number of words used.

title: Balanced Ternary Nonzero Digits
description: Every integer has a unique balanced ternary representation, a sum of terms `d * 3^i` with each digit `d` equal to `-1`, `0` or `1`. Return the number of non-zero digits in the representation of `n` (it is `0` for `n = 0`).
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Negabinary Representation
description: In base `-2` (negabinary) the digits are `0` and `1` and the digit at position `i` (counting from the right, starting at 0) has weight `(-2)^i`. Every integer has a unique representation without leading zeros (`0` is written `0`). Return the representation of `n` as a string.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Elias Omega Code Length
description: The Elias omega code of a positive integer `n` is built like this: start with the string `0`; while `n > 1`, put the binary representation of `n` (without leading zeros) in front of the string and replace `n` by the number of bits of that binary representation minus one. Return the length of the finished code for `n`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Convolution Output Sum
description: A grayscale image is stored row by row in `pixels` with `cols` pixels per row. A `3 x 3` filter `kernel` (nine weights stored row by row) is slid over every position where it fits completely inside the image; at each position the output is the sum of `kernel[a][b]` times the pixel under it for all `a, b` in `0..2` (no flipping). Return the sum of all outputs.
constraints: pixels form a rectangular image with at least 3 rows and 3 columns, at most 400 pixels, values 0 to 255

title: Max Pooling Total
description: A grayscale image is stored row by row in `pixels` with `cols` pixels per row. Max pooling with window size `s` cuts the image into non-overlapping `s x s` windows starting at the top-left corner (rows and columns that do not fill a complete window at the right or bottom edge are dropped) and keeps the largest pixel of each window. Return the sum of the kept values.

examples.explanation: The pooled values add up to 4.
The pooled values add up to 7.

constraints: pixels form a rectangular image of at most 10000 pixels, values 0 to 255

title: Rectangle Query Sum Total
description: A grayscale image is stored row by row in `pixels` with `cols` pixels per row. `queries` is a flat list of rectangles `[r1, c1, r2, c2, ...]` (0-based, both corners inclusive, `r1 <= r2` and `c1 <= c2`). Each query asks for the sum of the pixels inside its rectangle. Return the sum of the answers of all queries.
constraints: pixels form a rectangular image of at most 400 pixels, values 0 to 255
1 <= queries.length / 4 <= 50 and every rectangle lies inside the image

title: Edge Pixel Count
description: A grayscale image is stored row by row in `pixels` with `cols` pixels per row. A pixel is an edge pixel if its value differs by more than `t` from the pixel to its right or from the pixel below it (neighbours outside the image are ignored). Return the number of edge pixels.
constraints: pixels form a rectangular image of at most 10000 pixels, values 0 to 255

title: Quarter Turn Weighted Sum
description: A grayscale image is stored row by row in `pixels` with `cols` pixels per row. Rotate the image 90 degrees clockwise (the left column becomes the top row, read bottom to top), write the rotated image out row by row, and return the sum over all positions `k` (0-based) of `k` times the pixel value at position `k`.
constraints: pixels form a rectangular image of at most 400 pixels, values 0 to 255
All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Row Run Total
description: A grayscale image is stored row by row in `pixels` with `cols` pixels per row. In each row, a run is a maximal block of consecutive pixels with the same value (runs never continue from one row into the next). Return the total number of runs over all rows.
constraints: pixels form a rectangular image of at most 10000 pixels, values 0 to 255
All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Median Filter Output Sum
description: A grayscale image is stored row by row in `pixels` with `cols` pixels per row. A median filter replaces each interior pixel (one that has all eight neighbours) by the median of the nine values in its `3 x 3` neighbourhood, the fifth smallest value. Return the sum of the filtered values of all interior pixels.

examples.explanation: The filtered interior adds up to 5.
The filtered interior adds up to 0.

constraints: pixels form a rectangular image with at least 3 rows and 3 columns, at most 400 pixels, values 0 to 255
All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Sobel Edge Strength Peak
description: A grayscale image is stored row by row in `pixels` with `cols` pixels per row. For each interior pixel (one with all eight neighbours) the Sobel filter computes `Gx`, the sum of the right column's three neighbours weighted `1, 2, 1` (top to bottom) minus the same weighted sum of the left column, and `Gy`, the sum of the bottom row's three neighbours weighted `1, 2, 1` (left to right) minus the same weighted sum of the top row. The edge strength of the pixel is `|Gx| + |Gy|`. Return the largest edge strength over all interior pixels.
constraints: pixels form a rectangular image with at least 3 rows and 3 columns, at most 400 pixels, values 0 to 255
All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Best Overlay Shift Overlap
description: Two binary images `a` and `b` of the same size are stored row by row with `cols` pixels per row (each pixel is 0 or 1). Image `b` may be shifted by any whole number of rows and columns (up and down, left and right) over image `a`; parts of `b` that leave the frame are ignored. For a shift, the overlap is the number of positions where both images show a `1`. Return the largest overlap over all shifts.
constraints: a and b are rectangular images of equal size with at most 100 pixels each, values 0 or 1
All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Farthest From Bright Pixel
description: A binary image is stored row by row in `pixels` with `cols` pixels per row (each pixel is 0 or 1). The distance between two cells is the Manhattan distance (rows apart plus columns apart). For every cell take the distance to the nearest pixel equal to 1 (that distance is 0 for the pixels equal to 1). Return the largest such distance over all cells, or `-1` if the image has no 1.

examples.explanation: The farthest cell is 2 steps from a bright pixel (-1 means no bright pixel).
The farthest cell is -1 steps from a bright pixel (-1 means no bright pixel).

constraints: pixels form a rectangular image of at most 10000 pixels, values 0 or 1
All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Stack Machine Result
description: A stack machine runs a program given as space-separated tokens. `PUSH d` (where `d` is a digit `0` to `9`, written as the next token) pushes `d`. `DUP` pushes a copy of the top value, `POP` removes the top value and `SWAP` exchanges the top two values. `ADD`, `SUB` and `MUL` remove the top value `b` and then the next value `a` and push `a + b`, `a - b` or `a * b`. Return the value on top of the stack when the program ends. The program is valid: it never takes values from an empty stack and it leaves at least one value.

examples.explanation: The top of the stack is 7.
The top of the stack is 25.

constraints: the program only uses the tokens above and is valid

title: Register Machine Step Count
description: A tiny machine has registers `a`, `b` and `c`, all starting at 0, and runs a program given as instructions separated by semicolons (the first instruction has index 0). `inc r` adds 1 to register `r`, `dec r` subtracts 1, `cpy n r` sets register `r` to the integer `n`, and `jnz r k` jumps `k` instructions forward (or backward when `k` is negative) relative to itself if register `r` is not zero, otherwise it moves on to the next instruction. The program stops when the next instruction index lies outside the program. Return the number of instructions executed, or `-1` if more than 10000 instructions would be executed.

examples.explanation: The machine executes 7 instructions (-1 means it did not stop in time).
The machine executes 2 instructions (-1 means it did not stop in time).

constraints: numbers in cpy are between -999 and 999 and jump offsets are non-zero numbers between -99 and 99

args: cpy 5 a;cpy 0 b;inc b;dec a;jnz a -2
cpy 2 a;cpy 3 b;inc c;dec b;jnz b -2;dec a;jnz a -5

title: Linear Probing Last Slot
description: A hash table has `m` slots numbered `0..m-1`. A key `k` is inserted into slot `k mod m`; if that slot is taken, the next slots `(k + 1) mod m, (k + 2) mod m, ...` are tried in order until a free one is found. Keys are inserted in the order of `keys`. Return the slot used by the last key, or `-1` if some key arrives when the table is already full (then it cannot be inserted).

examples.explanation: The last key lands in slot 3 (-1 means the table overflowed).
The last key lands in slot 2 (-1 means the table overflowed).

title: Quadratic Probing Failures
description: A hash table has `m` slots numbered `0..m-1`. A key `k` is tried in slots `(k + i*i) mod m` for `i = 0, 1, ..., m-1` in this order and placed into the first free one; if all of these `m` slots are occupied the key is dropped (insertion fails). Keys are inserted in the order of `keys`. Return the number of keys whose insertion fails.

title: Merge Sort Comparison Count
description: Top-down merge sort splits an array of length `n` into a left half of `n / 2` elements (rounded down) and a right half holding the rest, sorts both halves recursively, and merges them: while both halves still have elements it compares the front elements, taking the left one if it is less than or equal to the right one and the right one otherwise; once one half is empty the remainder of the other half is copied without comparisons. Return the total number of element comparisons made while sorting `nums`.

title: Quick Sort Comparison Count
description: Quick sort with the Lomuto partition scheme sorts `nums[lo..hi]` as follows: take `nums[hi]` as the pivot; keep a boundary `i = lo - 1`; for `j` from `lo` to `hi - 1`, compare `nums[j]` with the pivot and, if `nums[j] <= pivot`, increase `i` and swap `nums[i]` with `nums[j]`; finally swap `nums[i + 1]` with the pivot and recursively sort the parts on both sides of the pivot's final position. Every comparison of an element with the pivot counts once. Return the total number of comparisons made while sorting the whole array.

title: Heap Construction Swap Count
description: A max-heap is built from `nums` (stored as an array where the children of index `i` are `2i + 1` and `2i + 2`) by sifting down every non-leaf node from index `n/2 - 1` (rounded down) back to index 0. Sifting a node down means: while it has a child larger than itself, swap it with its larger child (the left child if the children are equal) and continue from that child's position. Return the total number of swaps performed.

title: Polynomial Product Coefficient
description: Two polynomials are given by their coefficients from the constant term upward (`a[i]` multiplies `x^i`). Return the coefficient of `x^k` in their product (it is `0` when `k` is larger than the degree of the product).

title: Common Working Minutes
description: People in different time zones all work from 09:00 (inclusive) to 17:00 (exclusive) in their own local time, every day. `offsets[i]` is person `i`'s time zone offset from UTC in minutes (positive means ahead of UTC, so local time is UTC plus the offset, modulo 24 hours). Consider one UTC day of 1440 minutes (minute `0` is 00:00 UTC). Return the number of minutes of that day, taken in the cyclic sense (the day repeats forever), during which every person is working.

examples.explanation: All of them are working during 480 minutes.
All of them are working during 420 minutes.

title: Working Hours Finish Time
description: Work is only done between 09:00 and 17:00 on every day (8 working hours per day, no days off). A task needing `T` whole working hours starts at the beginning of hour `h` on day `day`; if that moment is outside working hours the task waits until 09:00 of the first working period that follows. Return the finishing time as `day * 100 + hour`, where `hour` is the clock hour at which the task finishes (between 10 and 17). A task finishing exactly at 17:00 finishes on that day, at hour 17.

title: Local DNA Alignment Score
description: A local alignment pairs up a substring of `a` with a substring of `b`, possibly inserting gaps. Each aligned pair of equal letters scores `+2`, each aligned pair of different letters scores `-1`, and each letter left against a gap scores `-1`. The score of an alignment is the sum over all its positions, and the empty alignment scores `0`. Return the best score over all local alignments of `a` and `b`.
constraints: a and b consist of A, C, G and T

title: Polynomial GCD Degree
description: Two non-zero polynomials with integer coefficients are given from the constant term upward (`a[i]` multiplies `x^i`), and the last coefficient of each list is non-zero. Consider their greatest common divisor as polynomials over the rational numbers. Return its degree (a degree of `0` means the polynomials have no common factor except constants).
constraints: -9 <= a[i], b[i] <= 9 and the last coefficient of each list is non-zero

title: Determinant Modulo Prime
description: An `n x n` integer matrix is given row by row in a flat array `m` (entry `(i, j)` is `m[i*n + j]`). Return its determinant modulo `1000000007`, as a value in `[0, 1000000006]`.

title: Xor Span Dimension
description: Treat every number in `a` as a vector of bits over the field with two elements, where addition is XOR. The span of the list is the set of all values obtainable by XOR-ing any sub-collection of its numbers (the empty collection gives `0`). The dimension of the span is the base-2 logarithm of its size. Return that dimension.

title: Sorting Network Check
description: A comparator network on `n` wires is given as a flat list of pairs `net = [i1, j1, i2, j2, ...]` with `i < j` in each pair. Applying a pair compares the values on wires `i` and `j` and swaps them if the value on wire `i` is larger, so the smaller one ends on wire `i`. The pairs are applied in the given order. Return `true` if the network turns every possible input sequence into a non-decreasing one, otherwise `false`.
constraints: net.length is even and 0 <= i < j < n for every pair

title: Stable Matching Partner
description: There are `n` men and `n` women, numbered from `0`. Preference lists are flat arrays: `mp[i*n + j]` is the woman that man `i` ranks in position `j` (position `0` is the favourite), and `wp[i*n + j]` is the man that woman `i` ranks in position `j`. A matching is stable when no man and woman both prefer each other to their current partners. Among all stable matchings, take the one that is best for the men (every man gets the best partner he can have in any stable matching). Return the woman matched to man `0` in it.

examples.explanation: In the men-optimal stable matching man 0 gets woman 0.
In the men-optimal stable matching man 0 gets woman 0.

constraints: mp and wp each hold n lists that are permutations of 0..n-1

title: Cube Face Colorings
description: Each of the six faces of a cube is painted with one of `k` colors. Two paintings count as the same if one can be turned into the other by rotating the cube in space (reflections are not allowed). Return the number of distinct paintings modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: Only the 24 rotations of the cube are allowed

title: Fibonacci Nim Opening Win
description: A pile has `n` stones. Two players alternate; the first player must take at least one stone but not the whole pile. After that, each player must take at least one stone and at most twice the number of stones the previous player just took. The player who takes the last stone wins. Both play optimally. Return `true` if the first player wins.
constraints: Players must take at least 1 stone each turn

title: Lights Out Minimum Presses
description: A grid of lights is stored row by row in `g` (`cols` lights per row), where `1` is on and `0` is off. Pressing a light toggles it and its up, down, left and right neighbours that exist. Return the minimum number of presses that turns every light off, or `-1` if that is impossible.

examples.explanation: The minimum number of presses is 5.
The minimum number of presses is 0.

constraints: g.length is a multiple of cols and every g[i] is 0 or 1

title: Standard Young Tableaux Count
description: A Young diagram has rows of lengths `shape[0] >= shape[1] >= ...`, left-aligned. A standard filling writes each number from `1` to the total number of cells exactly once so that every row increases left to right and every column increases top to bottom. Return the number of standard fillings modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: shape is non-increasing, shape[i] >= 1 and the sum of shape is at most 1000

title: Diagonal Safe Step Paths
description: A walker starts at `(0, 0)` and must reach `(n, n)`. In one move it may go right `(+1, 0)`, up `(0, +1)`, or diagonally `(+1, +1)`. At every point `(x, y)` on the way it must satisfy `y <= x`. Return the number of different paths modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: Moves are right, up and diagonal only

title: Mountain Walks With Exact Sea-Level Returns
description: A hiker takes `2n` steps, each one up or one down in altitude, starting at altitude `0`, never going below `0`, and finishing at altitude `0`. Each time the hiker arrives at altitude `0` after a step (including the final step) counts as one return. Return the number of such walks that have exactly `k` returns, modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: A walk never goes below altitude 0

title: RNA Maximum Base Pairs
description: An RNA strand is a string over `A`, `C`, `G`, `U`. Two positions `i < j` can be paired if their letters are `A`-`U` or `G`-`C` (in either order) and `j - i >= 4`. A folding is a set of pairs where every position is in at most one pair and no two pairs cross (there is no `a < x < b < y` with `(a, b)` and `(x, y)` both chosen). Return the maximum number of pairs in a folding.
constraints: s consists of A, C, G and U

title: Wildcard Star Pattern Matching
description: Implement matching of a whole string `s` against a pattern `p`. In `p`, `.` matches any single character and a letter matches itself. A `*` always follows another symbol and means that symbol may repeat zero or more times. The match must cover all of `s`. Return `true` if `p` matches `s`.
constraints: s has lowercase letters; p has lowercase letters, '.' and '*', where every '*' follows a letter or '.'

title: Tree Maximum Weight Matching
description: A tree has nodes `0..n-1` where `n = par.length + 1`. For each `i`, node `i + 1` is joined to its parent `par[i]` (with `par[i] <= i`) by an edge of weight `w[i]`. Choose a set of edges so that no node belongs to two chosen edges. Return the largest possible total weight (choosing no edges gives `0`).

examples.explanation: The best matching has total weight 5.
The best matching has total weight 4.

title: Cuckoo Hashing First Failure
description: A hash table has `m` slots and holds at most one key per slot. Every key `x` may live in exactly one of two candidate slots: `x % m` or `(x / m) % m` (integer division). Keys are inserted one by one, and an insertion may move earlier keys between their two candidate slots to make room. Return the 0-based index of the first key after which it is impossible to place all keys inserted so far, or `-1` if every key can be placed.

examples.explanation: The first impossible insertion is at index -1.
The first impossible insertion is at index -1.

title: Extend Polynomial Sequence
description: A polynomial `P` of degree less than `n = ys.length` satisfies `P(i) = ys[i]` for `i = 0..n-1` (it is the unique such polynomial with rational coefficients). Given `x`, return `P(x)` modulo `1000000007`, as a value in `[0, 1000000006]`. The value `P(x)` is always an integer.

title: Union Find Rollback Component Sum
description: There are `n` nodes `0..n-1`, initially all separate. `ops` is a flat list of triples `(t, a, b)`. If `t = 0`, connect `a` and `b` (this still counts as an applied connection even when they were already connected). If `t = 1`, undo the most recent connection that has not been undone yet (ignore `a` and `b`; do nothing if there is none). After each operation, count the connected components. Return the sum of these counts over all operations, modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The sum of component counts is 1.
The sum of component counts is 3.

constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000 and 3 <= ops.length <= 300000, ops.length is a multiple of 3
t is 0 or 1 and 0 <= a, b < n

title: Roadside Depot Placement Cost
description: Houses stand along a straight road at positions `xs`. You will build exactly `k` depots (each depot may be placed at any integer position) and every house walks to its nearest depot. Return the minimum possible total walking distance of all houses.

examples.explanation: The minimum total walking distance is 2.
The minimum total walking distance is 0.

title: Spanning Tree Count
description: An undirected multigraph has `n` nodes `0..n-1` and its edges are given as flat pairs `edges = [a1, b1, a2, b2, ...]`. Parallel edges are different edges and count separately; self-loops never appear. Return the number of spanning trees (sets of `n - 1` edges that connect all nodes) modulo `1000000007`. A graph that is not connected has `0`; a single node has `1`.

examples.explanation: The graph has 1 spanning trees modulo 1000000007.
The graph has 3 spanning trees modulo 1000000007.

constraints: 1 <= n <= 50 and edges.length is even and at most 2000
0 <= a, b < n and a != b for every edge

title: Square Grid Rotation Colorings
description: Every cell of an `n x n` grid is painted with one of `k` colors. Two paintings are considered the same if one becomes the other after rotating the whole grid by a multiple of 90 degrees (reflections are not allowed). Return the number of different paintings modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: Only the four rotations of the square are allowed

title: Non-Attacking Rook Placements
description: A board is stored row by row in `board` (`cols` cells per row); a cell holding `1` may receive a rook and a cell holding `0` may not. Return the number of ways to place exactly `k` rooks on allowed cells so that no two rooks share a row or a column, modulo `1000000007`. Placements are different if the sets of occupied cells differ.
constraints: 0 <= k <= 12, board.length is a multiple of cols and board[i] is 0 or 1

title: Boolean Expression Parenthesizations
description: `s` is a boolean expression made of the operands `T` (true) and `F` (false) separated by the binary operators `&` (and), `|` (or) and `^` (xor), for example `T|F&T`. Count the ways to fully parenthesize the expression (choosing which operator is applied last, recursively) so that it evaluates to true. Different parenthesizations are different even if they give the same shape of values. Return the count modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: There are 1 ways to evaluate to true.
There are 0 ways to evaluate to true.

constraints: s alternates operands in 'TF' and operators in '&|^', starting and ending with an operand

title: Distinct Common Subsequences
description: Return the number of different non-empty strings that are a subsequence of both `a` and `b`. Two subsequences that read the same count once, no matter how many ways they can be picked. Give the answer modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The two strings share 7 distinct subsequences.
The two strings share 1 distinct subsequences.

constraints: a and b consist of the letters a, b and c

title: Three-String Longest Common Subsequence
description: Return the length of the longest string that is a subsequence of all three strings `a`, `b` and `c` (a subsequence keeps the relative order of characters but may skip some).

examples.explanation: The longest common subsequence has length 3.
The longest common subsequence has length 0.

constraints: a, b and c consist of lowercase letters
